location: Proof of thm:coherence:cpc, paragraph 'Explicit finite bases' (and the parenthetical in coherence.tex Thm 6.15(a))
problem: The paper's formulas include primitive constants ⊥ and ⊤ (setting.tex §2.1; also the Lean language), and the coherence datum is A_0 ⊬_h ⊥. The displayed basis is the Łukasiewicz axioms, the ∧/∨ →-axioms and MP, with no axiom about ⊥ or ⊤. So ⊥ behaves as an unsubstitutable atom: ⊢¬⊥, ⊢⊤ and ⊢⊥→p are not in ⟨D⟩, and the proof's conclusion 'Hence ⟨D⟩=Cn_2' is false in the paper's language. Round-2 re-verification flagged this (T2 'Thm 3.3(a), revised example basis', item (1)). It was not repaired, and Lean does not formalize the finite-basis clause.
proposed_fix:
After '...$\step(p	o r)	o((q	o r)	o(p\vee q	o r))$.' insert: 'If $ ot$ or $	op$ is a primitive constant, add the axioms $\step
eg ot$, resp. $\step	op$; with the third axiom and $K$ these give $\step ot	o p$.' In the Kalmár sentence add 'and $\vdash
eg ot$, $\vdash	op$ (base cases for the constants)'. In coherence.tex Thm 6.15(a) change the parenthetical to '(with $	o$ in the language, Hilbert-style bases with modus ponens as the only rule, plus $\step
eg ot$ and $\step	op$ when these constants are primitive; ...)'.

location: Caption of tab:coherence:rank ('they exclude only meanings realizing no certified position')
problem: Wrong quantifier. A certification of ⟨A|D⟩ excludes every meaning that fails to realize that particular position, so a meaning is excluded as soon as it misses some certified position, not only when it realizes none. Example: certifying ⟨χ,¬χ| ⟩ excludes BV. Round 2 flagged this (T2 Sec 4.2 reading (i)).
proposed_fix: Replace the second caption sentence with: 'Coherence \emph{certifications} are positive data about meanings: certifying $\pos AD$ excludes exactly the meanings that do not realize $\pos AD$ (for the empty position, only $V=\emptyset$), and adding $\valtop$ to a meaning never makes it fail a certification.'

location: thm:coherence:telltale (d): 'Without structurality BV is not identifiable in the limit at all, even with the coherence datum'
problem: The proof, and Lean BV_not_BC_learnable, cover text plus the single target-independent datum ⟨ | ⟩. With all target-certified positions supplied, text plus certifications is an informant (cf. prop:coherence:informant). Then ⟨χ,¬χ| ⟩ separates BV∪{v'_χ} from BV and the class becomes identifiable. 'At all' therefore overclaims. Round 2 flagged this (T2 Thm 4.4(d)).
proposed_fix: Replace with 'Without structurality $\BV$ is not identifiable in the limit from text plus the coherence datum $\pos{\ }{\ }$, or any other target-independent certifications:'. Append: '(If every target-certified position is supplied, text plus certifications is an informant, as in \Cref{prop:coherence:informant}, and this obstruction disappears.)'. Adjust the 'Non-learnability' paragraph in app-coherence.tex the same way.

location: Reading after prop:coherence:complete: '(Whether a fixed finite family of contexts suffices for RCF is open.'
problem: Round-2 re-verification (T2 Prop 3.11(c)) notes this is settled negatively. Each context in a finite family 𝒜 defines a semialgebraic set over ℚ whose components contain points with algebraic coordinates of degree ≤ D(𝒜). A term forced to be a root of f is constant on components, so it takes such a value. For even d > D′(𝒜), the rule t^d=1+1 ▷ t>0 (Eisenstein, degree-d root) therefore never fires in a designated context or from ∅. It is coherent on 𝒜 yet unsound (c=−2^{1/d}).
proposed_fix: Replace the sentence with: '(No fixed finite family of contexts suffices: the rule $t^{d}=1+1\step t>0$ with $d$ even and large enough never fires in any context of the family, because points of semialgebraic sets defined over $\mathbb Q$ have algebraic coordinates of bounded degree, so it is coherent on the family but unsound; this observation is due to the second-round referee.)', or delete the sentence.

location: thm:coherence:residue (iii) (and app-coherence.tex proof of (iii))
problem: §6.3 fixes 'Hypotheses are r.e. theories', but (iii) lists 'PA+¬Con(PA) and its non-standard completions', which are not r.e. Also, 'the sound T_k ... remain, and cannot be discriminated' overstates thm:coherence:turing. Distinct T_j, T_k are separated by text; what fails is identification of the chain together with T_ω. Round 2 flagged both points (T2 Thm 6.4(iii)).
proposed_fix: Replace (iii) with: '$\mathcal G$ deductive closure, $\hstar=\PA$, $\Ac=\{\emptyset\}$: $\Alt$ is the set of all consistent closed extensions of $\PA$ (the r.e. ones, if hypotheses are r.e.), e.g. $\PA+\neg\Con(\PA)$, whose completions (not r.e.) have only non-standard models. Designating all finite sets of true sentences removes exactly the unsound ones; the sound $T_k$ of \Cref{thm:coherence:turing} remain, and by that theorem no learner identifies them together with $T_\omega$ from text plus true-context coherence.' Make the matching change in the appendix.

location: ex:coherence:survivors (4), last sentence: 'The per-law converse is not Clark's completion, which is consistent there.'
problem: This holds only if rain and sprinkler are treated as abducibles, i.e. only the head wet is completed. Clark's full completion also makes the clause-less predicates false (¬rain, ¬sprinkler), which is inconsistent with A={wet}. Round 2 flagged this (T2 §6 example 4).
proposed_fix: Replace with: 'The per-law converse is not Clark's completion \citep{clark1978negation}: completing only the head $\mathit{wet}$ (with $\mathit{rain},\mathit{sprinkler}$ abducible) gives $\mathit{wet}\leftrightarrow\mathit{rain}\vee\mathit{sprinkler}$, which is consistent there.'

location: Reading after tab:coherence:rank: 'A testable prediction ...: imitation plus a contradiction penalty yields consistent but noncommittal reasoners.'
problem: thm:coherence:carnap and thm:coherence:rank show only that such data do not exclude gappy valuations ('provably free to settle on'). They give no reason to expect that training yields them, so 'yields' is an overclaim.
proposed_fix: Replace with: 'A testable question for language-model training: imitation plus a contradiction penalty does not rule out consistent but noncommittal reasoners; whether training drifts toward them is empirical.'

location: Proof of prop:coherence:tradeoff (b), final parenthetical 'Equivalently, by \cref{prop:coherence:oligarchy}, detection-halving needs R̂ ⊆ h_i ∩ h_j ...'
problem: This equivalence holds only under the worst-case hypothesis of prop:coherence:oligarchy, that every finite P ⊆ R̂ with P ⊄ ∩VS is a possible detection. Part (b) itself uses a genuine ⊥-derivation, and under that reading the 'needs' claim is false. Round 2 flagged this (T2 Prop 2.9(e)).
proposed_fix: Begin the sentence with: 'Under the worst-case hypothesis of \cref{prop:coherence:oligarchy} (every finite $P\subseteq\hat R$ with $P\not\subseteq\bigcap\VS$ is a possible detection), detection-halving needs ...'.

location: line 171 ('accepted all 13 valid and refuted all 44 invalid structural candidate schemas ... (computed; quick run)') and line 421 ('Experiment B shows the negative-data role end to end (computed; quick run) ... removed every unsound rule ... the adversary proved none of its goals'); also lines 191, 367 and the header comment
problem: These report a single quick smoke-test run (prop_learning_quick.md: one run at N=50) instead of the full grid used in §§7 and 12. The full grid has 177 candidates (59 valid, 118 invalid). With noise 'both' at N∈{50,100,200}, coherence leaves 1.2±0.9 unsound rules and 1.7±4.1 exploits; 19 of 72 runs end with an unsound rule after coherence. The claim that coherence 'removed every unsound rule' overstates the full results and contradicts §12.
proposed_fix: Line 171: '...a bold learner over classical natural deduction accepted all 59 valid and refuted all 118 invalid structural candidate schemas (of 177), each by an explicit derivation of ⊢⊥ (median 2.5 steps for generalizations of target rules, 6 for random schemas), while the non-structural ⊢p survived all eight designated contexts (computed).' Line 421: 'Experiment B shows the negative-data role end to end (computed; \Cref{tab:experiments:prop}). With systematic fallacies (AC, DA and an illegitimate discharge, all cited as →E) and 5% corrupted steps, at N∈{50,100,200}, imitation ends with 45.6±19.3 unsound active rules, and the adversary derives ⊢⊥ in 9 of 9 runs. Coherence pruning on five designated contexts, with blame by a minimum-weight hitting set, leaves 1.2±0.9 unsound rules, closes every route to ⊢⊥ and keeps all 13 target rules. Over all 72 runs (N from 5 to 200), 19 still end with an unsound rule after coherence; most survivors are non-structural (38 of 45 mention specific atoms). At N≤10, AC itself can survive, because a small learned calculus cannot derive the contradiction.' In lines 191 and 367 drop 'quick run' (the same facts are in the full report), and cite prop_learning.md in the header comment.

location: line 312: 'A testable prediction for language-model training: imitation plus a contradiction penalty yields consistent but noncommittal reasoners.'
problem: Theorems coherence:carnap and coherence:rank show only that such data do not exclude gappy valuations, which is a non-identifiability result. They do not predict what a trained model converges to. Calling this a prediction derived from the theorem is a non sequitur.
proposed_fix: Replace with: 'A conjecture for language-model training, not implied by the theorem (which concerns identifiability, not training dynamics): imitation plus a contradiction penalty does not by itself push a learner toward committal (Boolean) valuations, so it may leave consistent but noncommittal reasoners.'

location: line 204 ('Whether a fixed finite family of contexts suffices for RCF is open.') and line 321 (thm:coherence:telltale(d): 'not identifiable in the limit at all, even with the coherence datum')
problem: Round-2 re-verification of T2 (reverification-round2.md) reports two things the paper does not reflect. A short argument settles the RCF question negatively. And the no-tell-tale argument for (d) covers only text plus the single coherence datum; with the full stream of certified positions the data form an informant. The paper still calls the first open and states the second without qualification.
proposed_fix: Line 204: '(A second-round referee sketched a negative answer, that no fixed finite family suffices without ∃-closure; we have not checked it.)' Alternatively, verify the argument and state it. Line 321: '...is not identifiable in the limit from text plus the single coherence datum: ...'.

location: line 71: \citep[as we recall the result; we have not re-checked its exact statement]{rautenberg1981two}

location: line 251 (proof of thm:coherence:trilemma); also twotier.tex:428, app-coherence.tex:136, app-twotier.tex:251: "Post's hierarchy theorem"
problem: The fact used, that a Σn-complete set is not Πn (strictness of the arithmetical hierarchy), is the Kleene–Mostowski hierarchy theorem; Post's theorem is the link between the hierarchy and Turing jumps. The name is non-standard and is never cited.
proposed_fix: At all four occurrences replace "Post's hierarchy theorem" with "the arithmetical hierarchy theorem \citep[\S57]{kleene1952introduction}". The key kleene1952introduction is already in bib/coherence.bib.

location: start of sec:coherence:arith (line 207, before 'Hypotheses are r.e. theories')
problem: The subsection opens with notation and does not state its findings.
proposed_fix: Insert: 'Arithmetic is where coherence stops being a complete test. Coherence with a $\Sigma_1$-complete base already does everything $\Delta_0$ world feedback can (\cref{lem:coherence:delta0}); no r.e.\ hypothesis is maximal, and Turing progressions are not identifiable (\cref{thm:coherence:rosser,thm:coherence:turing}). The right use of coherence is Popperian: it detects false $\Pi_1$ claims but not false $\Sigma_1$ claims, and no computable channel decides $\Sigma_2$ truth in the limit (\cref{thm:coherence:popper}).'
